quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
Stop. Only move when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop. Only move when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians may be crossing where you cannot see them. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street. Give blind pedestrians the right-of-way at all times.

questions.question: Which vehicles must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tank trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat.
Sport utility vehicles with four or more people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tank trucks carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped sign on a truck means the load is dangerous. These trucks must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes, with or without a red tip.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Stop even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all laws, signs, and signals. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe in fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time.
questions.explanation: Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. Only time will remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Bad weather makes it hard for others to see your vehicle. Headlights help other drivers see you. Turn on your low beam headlights if you use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Relax and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and concentrate on driving. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Follow speed limits and forgive other drivers.

questions.question: You want to turn right at the corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is about to cross in front of you. You should:

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need them.
Before you get in the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before moving your vehicle. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seat belt, and secure loose items. Do this before you drive.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distractions take your attention away from driving. They can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of the two-part seat belt system. Using just one part gives you much less protection. Buckle your lap belt even if your shoulder belt is automatic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from the left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you a yield sign is ahead. Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: If you get a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
Brake hard and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: If you get a blowout, ease off the gas. Let the vehicle slow down before you brake. Use light braking as the vehicle slows.

questions.question: If you see animals near the roadway:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move onto the road. More animals may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: When can you drive in a bike lane?

options.text: During rush hour if there are no cyclists in the lane.
When you are within 200 feet of a street corner where you plan to turn right.
When you need to pass a driver ahead who is turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are within 200 feet of a street corner where you plan to turn right.
questions.explanation: You may enter a bike lane up to 200 feet before turning right. Watch for cyclists or motorcyclists between your vehicle and the curb.

questions.question: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: You must wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: When can you drive in a bike lane?

options.text: 30 minutes after sunset or 30 minutes before sunrise.
On foggy days when visibility is low.
200 feet before making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet before making a turn.
questions.explanation: When turning right, you may enter the bike lane up to 200 feet before the corner or driveway. Do not drive in the bike lane at any other time.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. It appears a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Complete your turn only when the intersection is clear and the signal allows.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To pass safely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Only pass when you are sure you have enough space to safely change lanes. If you are unsure, wait until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through if the intersection is clear and it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through if the intersection is clear and it is safe.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed. Always yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and make sure it is clear before going.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when gates are up.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when gates are up.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warning signs, lights, or flaggers are present. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait for time to pass.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or showers cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Which of these dangerous driving behaviors is also illegal?

options.text: Wearing headsets that cover both ears.
Having interior lights on.
Using cruise control on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing headsets that cover both ears.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while wearing headsets or earbuds in both ears.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Keep to the right if you are driving slower than other traffic.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are slower than surrounding traffic. It is illegal to back up or make U-turns on interstates, so use the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are typically:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides of divided highways.

questions.question: To help others see you when it gets dark, use your:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights as darkness falls. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers.

questions.question: If you drive slower than traffic around you, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.
Improve traffic flow.
Show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Slow down for heavy traffic or bad weather. However, driving too slowly can block traffic flow and result in a ticket. Match traffic speed unless traffic exceeds the speed limit.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian crosses your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure they see you before proceeding.
Carefully drive around them.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the accelerator or brake to regain balance. Steer toward the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: When driving through work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Maintain your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.
